doc: FBL 0.11, section 4.9 (Reading in part), FR-002 and FR-004, written here: a stray '}' at the top level closes no block, and is skipped alone and reported fbl.unmatched-close at line 6 (rule 7); a top-level statement that does not parse is skipped to its line's end and reported fbl.unparsed-text at line 7, as FBL 0.9's recovery does (rule 2); a block comment that is never closed is trivia to the end of the body, reported fbl.unclosed-comment at line 8 (rule 8), so the declaration after it is no statement. The workspace before them is read.

steps.doc: Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read.
A set in the part that is read is planned as usual.
Undo puts back the bytes the edit replaced.
